findings.claim: The additive SSE terminal signal for term_rejected is unreachable in production: _resume_graph_background never broadcasts graph_complete/terminal on success; only _run_graph_background emits terminal and cannot produce terminal_state.

node_publish ignores the bool returned by update_video_publish; a 0-row write-back silently leaves the row pending with no log/error while the node reports success, re-creating the RELIABILITY-007 stuck-pending state.

Post-then-write-back ordering creates an inconsistency window: publisher POST executes before update_video_publish; if the DAO raises after 2xx, the Instagram post is live while the videos row remains pending and the run ends in graph_error. Cross-boundary atomicity limit, not partial DB write.

OAuth access tokens are placed in graph state and langgraph checkpoints persist full thread state at rest; pre-existing, not introduced by this diff. design.md:43 claim credentials never persisted is inaccurate for checkpointer-enabled environments.

The approved/rejected decision is implemented as three near-identical structural pairs (_route_after_idea_approval/_route_after_publish_approval, two add_conditional_edges mappings, two resume-payload builders) differing only in flag names.
node_publish discards the bool returned by update_video_publish; a failed (0-row) write-back is indistinguishable from a persisted one in the node's return contract.
The terminal state value term_rejected is a bare string literal duplicated across three modules with no shared constant; a rename in one module does not propagate.

Production comments/docstrings reference ephemeral process IDs (TCK-004/005, D-A..D-F, REQ-PTT-xx) that resolve only against openspec artifacts; approve_idea repeats the same D-E rationale three times around a five-line logic block.
This snapshot introduces a second httpx.AsyncClient fake implementation for node_publish that duplicates the existing FakeResponse/FakeAsyncClient + fake_http fixture in test_publish_wiring.py.

The snapshot delivers 1158 authored changed lines across 15 files in one transaction vs ~525 forecast with a 3-PR stacked split (each slice < 400); ~2.2x the forecast on which size:exception approval was based, and per-slice review isolation is not present in the reviewed snapshot.

node_publish discards the return value of update_video_publish; when the DAO reports 0 rows, the node returns success and the graph completes with the videos row silently un-updated — a no-op that looks like progress, contradicting the change's own honesty contract. No test covers the DAO-False path inside the node.

The API contract doc of record contradicts the implemented externally-visible contract: 3.3 documents ideas/approve as 200 OK; 3.4 documents publish/approve returning the fabricated published_post_id this change removed; neither documents the new 202/404/422 semantics.

The baseline claims (252->270 passed; single failure = test_scriptwriting_crew_4_blocks green standalone) cannot be verified from local artifacts; .pytest_cache predates the change and lastfailed names a different test.

The e2e lifecycle test invokes the REAL run_ideation_crew and run_scriptwriting_crew with no monkeypatching; both hit live external dependencies; determinism depends on each dependency's offline fallback.

test_run_scriptwriting_crew_4_blocks calls the real run_scriptwriting_crew with NO mock of agents.llm.acomplete (sibling tests do monkeypatch it); with an LLM reachable, output is nondeterministic. Mechanism for a pre-existing environment-dependent flake confirmed by code inspection.

Dead config: env key literally named AGENCY_ENV=dev: (contains = in key) set twice; harmless because correct AGENCY_ENV: dev is also set at line 14. CI pytest runs from repo root with no pytest.ini/pyproject.toml and no working-directory.

After POST 2xx with real published_post_id (irreversible external effect), update_video_publish runs with bare await: if the DAO raises, the run fails with generic graph_error and the videos row stays without instagram_post_id; if the DAO returns False, skip is fully silent. No retry/backoff or compensating action; recovery is manual re-approve (idempotency key dedupes re-POST).

New SSE signals graph_complete.terminal=term_rejected and graph_error.code=no_candidates have no consumer: useSSEStream.js registers only node_change/log_entry/checkpoint_paused/onerror; grep of terminal in frontend src gives 0 matches. A rejection ends the graph without visible feedback; checkpoint_paused stays true forever so UI shows paused card indefinitely.

The 404 path of approve_idea (0 rows) occurs before broadcast+resume: the langgraph thread stays paused at human_approval_idea without SSE signal, timeout, or cleanup; with thread_id=tenant_id, a later /graph/run resumes that checkpoint instead of starting fresh. Recovery manual only.

approve_publish does NOT persist the decision: publish_approval_status is written only as 'pending' in insert_video; no DAO/route transitions it to approved/rejected. The publish decision lives only in checkpointer state — asymmetric with approve_idea which commits (update_idea_approval). Thread state loss reverts approval to pending without DB trace.
findings.proof_refs: grep publish_approval_status: 14 matches, transitions only 'pending' (daos.py:135, video_edit.py:7); test_daos.py:312, test_node_writes.py:519

findings.claim: _resume_graph_background/_run_graph_background: single ainvoke, single try/except to graph_error. No retry/backoff for transient DB/saver blips; run lost (manual recovery). Degradation not silent (log + SSE error) and PG checkpointer saves progressively.

On resume with publish_rejected=True, node_human_approval_publish logs the waiting message ('Esperando aprobacion humana...') which the client consumes as log_entry, describing the opposite of the real state (rejection). Misleading diagnostics in the visible stream.
